# Where pyiceberg's extra time goes, on microsoft-onelake.
# Generated by bench_breakdown.py. Same catalog object, same session,
# same URL at every depth, so each line differs from the one above it
# by exactly one thing.

  client      pyiceberg 0.12.0 on python 3.14.7
  iterations  120, after 5 discarded
  measured    2026-09-18T16:49:33Z

## One GET /v1/{prefix}/namespaces, at three depths (microseconds)

  layer                      p50       p90     stdev    added p50    2xSEM  separable?
  transport only         36441.7   40892.9    4104.4           --       --
  transport, no env      35983.3   40577.4    4764.4       -458.4    869.9  NO -- noise
  + json.loads           36493.6   40681.2    7111.3       +510.3   1298.3  NO -- noise
  + pydantic             36354.8   40991.2    5752.5       -138.8   1298.3  NO -- noise
  + client method        36444.0   41195.2    3086.8        +89.2   1050.3  NO -- noise

  A delta is called separable only when it exceeds twice the standard
  error of the mean of the noisier layer it is differenced against.
  Anything marked NO is this machine, not that layer, and must not be
  quoted as the cost of it.

  transport is 100% of the call; everything the library does on top of
  it is the other 0%.

## The same GET through the other client's HTTP stack

  layer                      p50       p90     stdev
  rust, reqwest          35055.8   39536.9    4331.1
  python, requests       36441.7   40892.9    4104.4

  Both are a GET to the same URL with the same bearer, body read and
  discarded, against the same server, over the network, where the
  round trip is inside both. The server's own time is inside both of
  them, so the difference between these two lines is the HTTP client
  and nothing else.

  transport gap      +1385.9 us   95% bootstrap interval [-30.2, +2859.2]  NO -- interval spans zero
  pyiceberg's own    +2.3 us  (the client method above transport)

  Caveat: the Rust floor is one block run after the Python layers, not
  interleaved with them. On loopback the gap is several times the
  noise and survives that. Over the network a gap of a millisecond is
  within the drift of a round trip between two blocks a minute apart,
  so the interval above says the two blocks differed, not that the
  HTTP clients do. bench.py interleaves the clients round by round and
  is the measurement to read for that.

## Startup, decomposed (milliseconds, p50 of 5)

  bare interpreter, `python3 -c pass`            9.2
  + import pyiceberg.catalog.rest              350.6
    of which, the import itself                341.4
  catalog construction (config + auth)         493.8

  The benchmark's cold start figure is larger than these lines add up
  to because the worker imports more than the client: yaml, the
  conformance harness's auth provider and this directory's own modules
  are all on the path before a request is made. The point stands
  either way -- the dominant term is importing Python code, and it is
  paid before the client does anything.
